payload.title: What Are the Mexican Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: Mexican wedding traditions in wedding order, from the pedida de mano and the padrinos to the lazo, the arras, the Mass, mariachi and the tornaboda, with notes for Australians marrying in Mexico or at home.
key_takeaways: Padrinos and madrinas, the wedding sponsors, each carry a role in the ceremony, from the lazo and the arras to the kneeling cushions and the bouquet.
In Mexico the civil ceremony is the legal marriage, and a church wedding does not replace it, so couples who want a Mass plan both.

The lazo and the 13 arras coins sit inside the Catholic Mass, while the money dance, la víbora de la mar and the tornaboda, the party on the day after the wedding, belong to the celebration around it.
As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise a high degree of caution" in Mexico overall, with higher levels for some states.

faq.q: What are the most common Mexican wedding traditions?
faq.a: The padrinos and madrinas, the lazo and arras in the Mass, the civil ceremony, mariachi, the money dance, la víbora de la mar and the tornaboda.
It is the day after the wedding, and the party held on that day.

faq.q: What do padrinos and madrinas do at a Mexican wedding?
faq.a: They are the wedding sponsors. Each pair carries a role in the Mass, such as the rings, arras, lazo, bible or bouquet, and in some communities they keep watch over the couple after the wedding.

faq.q: What does the lazo mean at a Mexican wedding?
faq.a: The typical lazo is two rosaries joined to form one, placed over the couple at the nuptial blessing after the Our Father.

faq.q: Who traditionally pays for a Mexican wedding?
faq.a: There is no fixed rule. In many families the couple and their parents carry the main costs and sponsors give the item tied to their role, so talk it through early with both families.

faq.q: What is la víbora de la mar?
faq.a: A wedding dance in which guests run in a line beneath the couple's joined hands. With the couple, the víbora stands for the problems they will face, and they must stay together without letting go.

faq.q: Can Australians have a legal wedding in Mexico?
faq.a: Yes, through a civil ceremony at the Registro Civil, since a church wedding does not replace it. Smartraveller says that in most cases an overseas marriage is legally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. Check documents and fees with the registry and the Australian Embassy in Mexico City.
